name: Testing
one_liner: Test early and test often, concurrently with development, inside every iteration.
purpose: Agile testing activities should be iterative and incremental: applying the strategy of 'test early and test often' allows risks to be identified and addressed early in the project's lifecycle. Testing should occur in each iteration, beginning with the earliest builds, and one iteration can have several test cycles. PM²-Agile recommends two testing practices — Test Management and Concurrent Testing — and anchors completion in acceptance criteria defined for each Feature and Story.
meta: What must the solution accomplish before a requirement counts as implemented?

fields.what: Agile testing activities should themselves be iterative and incremental rather than a phase at the end.
fields.pollux: Every two-week iteration tests what it built.

fields.what: The strategy allows risks to be identified and addressed early in the project's lifecycle.
fields.pollux: Traceability defects surface in iteration 2, not before Release 3.

fields.what: Testing activities should occur in each iteration, beginning with the earliest builds of the system.
fields.pollux: Begins with the first exposure view in January 2029.

fields.what: Depending on the frequency of new builds, one iteration can have several test cycles.
fields.pollux: Multiple cycles inside a single fortnight when builds are frequent.

fields.what: Testing focuses on what the solution needs to accomplish before a requirement is considered implemented.
fields.pollux: Conflict 6 — 'implemented' and 'Done' are not the same thing.

fields.what: User testing and validation of rapid prototypes, even before code, further develop requirements with specific conditions of satisfaction.
fields.pollux: Lean UX prototypes are tested with analysts before development starts.

fields.what: Acceptance criteria define the boundaries of a work item and are used to confirm when it is completed.
fields.pollux: Nobody argues with Marie Curie's acceptance criteria.

fields.what: A structured reference model covering the tools used in planning, designing, implementing, executing, evaluating and managing test work.
fields.who: ATeMs responsible for the Test Plan
fields.pollux: Documented in the Test Plan the ATeMs draft and you approve.

fields.what: The tools used for test tasks and work products need to align with the organisation's current practices.
fields.pollux: ESM tooling standards apply to the portal's test assets.

fields.what: Adopts testing concurrent with development throughout each iteration, preventing teams from compressing testing into a separate end-of-iteration activity.
fields.pollux: No test week before each quarterly release date.

fields.what: It reinforces feature teams working in parallel and requires high integration and high-bandwidth communication between developers and testers.
fields.pollux: Possible because every ATeM tests; there is no separate test team.

fields.what: Consider testing-related activities in parallel with requirements gathering and refinement so team and stakeholders agree conditions of satisfaction.
fields.pollux: Conditions of satisfaction agreed during refinement, not after the demo.

fields.f: Criteria for each Feature and Story
fields.what: Ensuring acceptance criteria are defined for each Feature and Story lets the team check delivery against users' expectations.
fields.pollux: Each exposure view has criteria before it enters an iteration.

fields.f: Run tests as frequently as possible
fields.what: Ideally all tests run against each build deployed to the mainline; otherwise run regression tests and focus on the new build's items.
fields.pollux: Regression protects Release 1 behaviour while Release 2 is built.

fields.what: Even test scripts that are expected to fail provide valuable feedback about the state of the solution.
fields.pollux: Expected failures mark the work not yet started, honestly.

fields.what: Once a test script passes, it should not fail against subsequent builds of the solution.
fields.pollux: A reconciliation test that passed in June must still pass in September.

traps: Concurrent testing exists to stop testing being compressed into the iteration's end.
Acceptance criteria are per Feature and Story; the Definition of Done is the team's standard.
Testing is every ATeM's job; an Independent Tester team is optional and extra.
A test script that has passed must never fail against later builds.
User testing of rapid prototypes can happen even before any code exists.
